topic: Throttled Gateways Multiply Distributed Retry Storms
postText:
A 200ms latency blip in our healthcare IT medication system recently escalated into a cluster-wide service blackout.

Our API Gateway had standard token bucket rate limiting. Downstream services had circuit breakers enabled. On paper, bulletproof architecture. In production, a textbook self-inflicted outage.

When a downstream service degraded, internal circuit breakers tripped. The gateway began serving 429 Too Many Requests and 503 errors. Because frontend apps and automated medical telemetry carts lacked exponential backoff with full jitter, thousands of clients instantly retried in synchronized loops.

The gateway spent its CPU verifying Redis token buckets and terminating TLS for retry traffic. Even worse: whenever bucket tokens replenished, micro-bursts bypassed the gateway directly into half-open downstream circuit breakers. This repeatedly reset failure thresholds, keeping vital clinical microservices trapped in perpetual death spirals.

Three fixes stabilized our infrastructure:
1. Jittered Retry-After: Never send naked 429s. Always emit dynamic Retry-After response headers with randomized intervals to desynchronize retrying clients.
2. Concurrency-Based Limiting: Enforce maximum in-flight requests per upstream route, rejecting excess before CPU burn occurs.
3. Adaptive Edge Load Shedding: When circuit breakers enter half-open states, configure the edge gateway to drop non-critical traffic immediately instead of queueing.

How do you coordinate edge rate limiting with circuit breaker recovery states across your services?
